what: The score combines exact insertion distance, a radial-savings reward, an order-insensitive route-versus-alternative-cluster affinity term, and a load-dependent one-customer capacity-packing lookahead. The insertion term chooses the slot; the remaining terms prioritize customers likely to belong to this route and avoid unusable residual capacity. Each invocation uses O(len(current route) + len(unassigned)) time and O(1) extra space.
why: Farthest-first route seeding benefits from continuing into the same remote geographic cluster rather than consuming nearby-depot customers first. The radial reward approximates avoided future depot travel, while the affinity term compares attachment to the current route with the customer's nearest capacity-compatible alternative among unassigned customers. This is useful when 2-opt can later reorder the route, because nearest-route affinity is less tied to the provisional sequence than insertion delta alone. The packing term becomes stronger as the route fills and favors residual capacities that another demand can nearly consume, which is relevant under the representative instances' mixed demands and capacity pressure. The coefficients are deliberately moderate and scale-free with respect to demand and geometry, but they are heuristic: nearest-neighbor affinity and one-step packing can miss broader cluster structure or multi-customer demand combinations, and no empirical improvement is claimed.
